hooks.text: Thirty men ran across the deck of the warship Vasa.
The warship Vasa failed its stability test before it ever sailed.
The pride of the Swedish Navy sank in twenty minutes.

title: Why Did the "Invincible" Vasa Sink in 20 Minutes? ⚠️
description: The Swedish warship Vasa was meant to be the pride of the Baltic, but a secret stability test proved it was a disaster waiting to happen.

beats.text: Thirty men ran across the deck of the warship Vasa.
beats.visual: Illustration of the Vasa ship stability test with men running, 1628

beats.text: Many believe this brand-new ship was a marvel of naval engineering.
beats.visual: Painting of the warship Vasa under full sail in Stockholm Harbor

beats.text: In reality, the 1628 stability test almost capsized the top-heavy vessel.
beats.visual: Cross-section illustration of the Vasa showing two full-length gundecks

beats.text: Vice Admiral Klas Fleming saw the ship teetering but stayed silent.
beats.visual: Portrait of Vice Admiral Klas Fleming

beats.text: Just 20 minutes into its maiden voyage, a light breeze struck.
beats.visual: Painting of the sinking of the Vasa in Stockholm Harbor

beats.text: Its fatal instability was proven when thirty men ran across the deck.
beats.visual: Reconstruction drawing of the Vasa ship stability test

better_than_last: This script applies the myth_vs_fact structure to emphasize the ignored stability test witnessed by Fleming.
